fields.meta_title: Feedback Form Builder and Question Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What a feedback form is, which questions to ask, and a free builder that routes every low rating to the person who can fix it.
fields.h1: Build a Feedback Form Someone Acts On
fields.hero_description: A feedback form collects a rating and a comment about one experience. Describe yours, and Emergent builds it with alerts for low scores and a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Feedback Form Should Do After Submit
fields.features_subheading: A template stops at the submit button. Emergent's version reads each answer and sends it to whoever can act on it.
fields.feature_1:
Star ratings with a follow-up question

Asks for a star rating, then shows a follow-up question that depends on the score. A 5-star answer is asked what went well, and a 2-star answer is asked what went wrong.
fields.feature_2:
Low scores routed to one owner

Sends a Slack or email alert to the owner of that order when a rating falls below the line you set. The alert carries the score and the comment, with a link back to the order.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on phones

Shows one question at a time on a phone, with the rating first and the comment box last. Required fields stay few, and anything optional is clearly marked as optional.
fields.feature_4:
A link and QR code per location

Creates a separate link for each store or event, plus a QR code you can print for the front counter. Each response records which link it came from without asking anyone.
fields.feature_5:
Responses in a database you own

Saves every response as a row in your own database, tagged with the date and the source. Filter a quarter of comments by location, or export them for the monthly review.
fields.feature_6:
Take the code with you

Exports the whole app to your GitHub on paid plans. An engineer can connect it to your CRM through its API and extend it, or you can describe the change and let Emergent write it.

fields.usecase_heading: Feedback Forms by Who Is Answering
fields.tab_content_1:
Two stars or fewer go straight to the support lead

A 2-star rating is worth more today than in next month's report. Seven days after delivery, the customer gets a form with a star rating and a comment box. Any rating of 2 stars or lower sends the support lead a direct message with the order and the comment. Every answer is saved to the orders database.
fields.tab_content_2:
One seller report from every visitor's answers

Sellers want to know what visitors thought of the price, not only how many came. A QR code at the door opens a form with 3 questions on the visitor's phone: price, condition, and interest. Answers add up per listing. The Sunday report showed the seller that 7 of 12 visitors found the asking price too high.
fields.tab_content_3:
Session scores by question, weakest first

A speaker improves fastest when the scores point at one thing to change. Attendees rate a workshop on clarity, pacing and usefulness, each on a 1 to 5 scale. When the form closes, the speaker sees the average for each question, lowest first. Pacing came in at 3.1, with comments asking for fewer slides.
fields.tab_content_4:
A flag for any wait over 30 minutes

Long waits are a complaint a clinic can fix once someone sees them by location. Two hours after a visit, the patient gets an emailed form about the wait and the staff. Any reported wait over 30 minutes flags the visit to the practice manager for that location, with the patient's comment attached.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Feedback Form
fields.howto_description: Good feedback forms are short, sent at the right moment and read by someone who can act. Seven steps, in the order you will meet them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers will change
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Cut it to five questions or fewer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask a follow-up based on the score
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decision the form should inform before writing a question: a delivery partner, a support script, a speaker's next talk. A form with no decision behind it collects opinions that sit unread. Write that decision at the top of your draft.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use 1 to 5 stars for satisfaction with one order or visit. Use 0 to 10 when you ask how likely someone is to recommend you, the Net Promoter Score question. Label both ends of the scale so every person reads them the same way.
fields.howto_step_3_des: One rating, one or two questions about the part you can change and one comment box cover most needs. Delete any question whose answer you would not act on. Make the comment box optional and put it last, after the rating.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Show a different second question to happy and unhappy people. Ask a 5-star customer what stood out, and ask a 2-star customer what went wrong. The low-score answers are the ones a team can act on the same week.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send it while the memory is fresh
fields.howto_step_5_des: Time the form to the experience: when a support ticket closes, a week after delivery, as a session ends, a couple of hours after an appointment. Fill in the order or visit from the link; nobody should have to type a reference number.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the person who handles each low rating and send it to them directly, with the score and the comment. A shared inbox lets everyone assume someone else replied. Track how long each low score waits before somebody responds.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Reply to the people who answered
fields.howto_step_7_des: Reply to anyone who left a low score and a comment, and tell them what changed. Once a month, read the comments by location or event and look for repeats. A problem named in ten comments deserves a fix.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Feedback Form Someone Acts On', title 'Feedback Form Builder and Question Examples' and hero 'A feedback form collects a rating and a comment about one experience' cover the whole job, not a sibling's.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is template galleries and explainers; page answers all 5 eligible PAA ('What is the feedback form?', 'How do I create a feedback form?', types, examples, another term), gives question examples (FAQ 6) and a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Tabs name the buyer's moments: 'Seven days after delivery', 'A QR code at the door', 'Pacing came in at 3.1', 'Any reported wait over 30 minutes flags the visit to the practice manager'.

openers.evidence: Every feature body opens on a verb ('Asks for a star rating', 'Sends a Slack or email alert', 'Creates a separate link'); tab paragraphs open on full sentences.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; sentences carry one idea ('Every answer is saved to the orders database.'); no blocking craft defect.

voice.evidence: Plain product verbs and unglamorous detail ('Order #10482', 'Box arrived crushed'); one templated tab-opener pattern kept as a note.

truth.evidence: NPS 0 to 10 matches the Bain source; broker open house matches Redfin; Emergent claims map to claims_used (alerts, conversational, no-caps, code-export on paid plans).

distinct.evidence: Tabs (orders, open houses, workshops, clinics) differ from training-feedback-form and anonymous-feedback-form tabs; siblings linked, not headlined.

faq.evidence: 10 real questions, hub link in item 2, sibling links 'employee feedback form', 'testimonial form', 'training feedback form'; each answer opens on the answer.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: 'Direct message to Dana Ruiz', '7 of 12 visitors: price too high' (7+4+1=12), 'Pacing averaged 3.1' lowest first, 'V-2292: 45-minute wait' flagged to the Midtown practice manager.
